title: Fermionic Villain model with exact lattice chiral symmetries
abstract: We present a fermionic lattice Hamiltonian that exactly realizes the $\mathrm{U(1)}_\mathrm{L}\times \mathrm{U(1)}_\mathrm{R}$ global symmetry and the associated chiral anomalies of a massless Dirac fermion in 1+1 dimensions. The construction couples Villain bosons to a Kitaev chain of Majorana fermions, where the bosonic fields are essential for evading Nielsen-Ninomiya-type no-go theorems. For two copies of our model, we realize the anomaly-free $\mathrm{U(1)}_{3450}$ global symmetry and construct symmetric boundary conditions. We analytically demonstrate symmetric mass generation by mapping the symmetry-preserving six-fermion interactions to fermion bilinear terms using fermionic T-duality. Finally, by gauging general anomaly-free global symmetries, we obtain a broad class of lattice chiral gauge theories. As nontrivial applications, we compute the mass spectra of the lattice Schwinger model and the 3450 gauge theory, finding agreement with the corresponding continuum results.
summary: This paper develops a fermionic lattice model called the Villain model that successfully incorporates exact chiral symmetries and anomalies on a lattice. By coupling Majorana fermions to bosonic fields, the authors overcome theoretical constraints and demonstrate methods like T-duality to achieve symmetric mass generation. This work provides a powerful framework for studying lattice chiral gauge theories.
main_problem: The central problem is constructing a fermionic lattice Hamiltonian that exactly realizes chiral global symmetries and their associated anomalies while overcoming constraints like the Nielsen-Ninomiya no-go theorem.
main_result: The authors successfully construct such a model, demonstrating anomaly cancellation and providing methods to generate mass symmetrically via T-duality mapping of six-fermion interactions.
method: The analysis employs techniques from lattice field theory, including the use of Villain bosons coupled to Majorana fermions, chiral charge quantization, and fermionic T-duality transformations.
model_or_system: The system is the 'fermionic Villain model,' which couples a Kitaev chain of Majorana fermions to bosonic Villain fields. The Hamiltonian is governed by Gauss law constraints that couple these bosonic and fermionic degrees of freedom.

important_parameters: The analysis explores various limits: continuum limit, deep infrared limit ($k=0$), and varying coupling strengths ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The construction relies on the bosonic Villain fields being essential to evade no-go theorems; T-duality is used as a key mathematical tool for mapping interactions.
